economic_context.claim: Austin's metropolitan economy produced $268.4B of output in 2024, spread across the five counties of the Austin metropolitan statistical area.
economic_context.caption: Total metro output for the Austin region, on Bureau of Economic Analysis data

economic_context.claim: Austin recorded 36.4% GDP growth between 2019 and 2024, the highest of any metropolitan area in the United States.
economic_context.caption: Five-year GDP growth for the Austin metro, the fastest of any US metro area

economic_context.claim: Texas produced a nominal GDP of $2.7 trillion in 2024, which would rank eighth in the world if Texas were a country.
economic_context.caption: Size of the Texas state economy, on the Governor's own published profile
economic_context.source_name: Office of the Texas Governor, Texas Economic Development and Tourism

economic_context.claim: Texas had a population of 31.3 million in 2024, growing at 1.8% a year against a United Kingdom population growing at 0.45%.
economic_context.caption: State population of Texas, growing four times faster than the United Kingdom
economic_context.source_name: Office of the Texas Governor, Texas Economic Development and Tourism

economic_context.claim: Edinburgh Airport delivered £2.7 billion of economic value to Scotland in 2025 and supported almost 44,000 jobs.
economic_context.caption: Economic value delivered to Scotland by Edinburgh Airport in a single year

economic_context.claim: Finance leads Edinburgh's local economy, generating £7.2 billion, as much as the next three largest sectors in the city combined.
economic_context.caption: Output of Edinburgh's largest sector, from the council's annual statistical review

economic_context.claim: Venture capital funding in Austin reached $7.94 billion in 2025, up 116.4% on 2024 and the fifth highest of any United States metro.
economic_context.caption: Venture capital raised by Austin-region companies in a record year

trade.claim: Trade between Texas and the United Kingdom totalled $20.6 billion in 2024, ranking the United Kingdom as Texas' eighth-largest trading partner.
trade.caption: Two-way goods trade between Texas and the United Kingdom in a single year
trade.source_name: Office of the Texas Governor, Texas Economic Development and Tourism

trade.claim: The United Kingdom was Texas' sixth-largest export destination in 2024, taking $14.8 billion of Texan goods.
trade.caption: Texas goods exported to the United Kingdom, its sixth-largest export market
trade.source_name: Office of the Texas Governor, Texas Economic Development and Tourism

trade.claim: United Kingdom companies reported 327 investment projects in Texas and $9.8 billion of capital investment over the decade to 2024, making the United Kingdom the leading source of foreign direct investment projects into the state.
trade.caption: British capital invested into Texas over ten years, the top source country by projects
trade.source_name: Office of the Texas Governor, Texas Economic Development and Tourism

trade.claim: British investment into Texas created more than 18,650 new jobs in the state over the decade to December 2024.
trade.caption: Texas jobs created by British investment projects over ten years
trade.source_name: Office of the Texas Governor, Texas Economic Development and Tourism

trade.claim: Texan companies reported 236 investment projects and $5.2 billion of capital investment into the United Kingdom over the same decade, so the investment runs in both directions.
trade.caption: Texan capital invested into the United Kingdom over ten years
trade.source_name: Office of the Texas Governor, Texas Economic Development and Tourism

trade.claim: Scotland's international exports were valued at £37.7 billion in 2023, with the United States its largest single-country destination.
trade.caption: Total value of Scotland's international exports, accredited Scottish statistics

trade.claim: The United States accounted for 17% of Scotland's international exports in 2023 and has been the top single-country destination every year since the series began in 2008.
trade.caption: US share of Scottish international exports, the leading country market since 2008

corporate_links.claim: Cirrus Logic, headquartered in Austin, employs approximately 350 people in Edinburgh, a team it acquired with Wolfson Microelectronics in 2014.
corporate_links.caption: Cirrus Logic's Edinburgh headcount, reporting to an Austin-headquartered business

corporate_links.claim: The Austin region employs more than 60,000 people in semiconductor related industries, with design centres run by Apple, ARM, Cirrus Logic, Intel, NVIDIA and Qualcomm.
corporate_links.caption: Semiconductor employment in the Austin region, the cluster Edinburgh design feeds

corporate_links.claim: The Austin region is home to more than 180 companies in semiconductor related industries.
corporate_links.caption: Semiconductor companies in the Austin region, a cluster dating to the 1970s

corporate_links.claim: Amazon's Development Centre Scotland in Edinburgh was the company's first development centre outside the United States, running machine learning and distributed systems engineering.
corporate_links.caption: Amazon's Edinburgh engineering centre, its first development site outside the US

corporate_links.claim: Accenture, Deloitte, Ernst and Young and PwC all appear on Austin's list of major regional employers, and each of the four also maintains an Edinburgh office.
corporate_links.caption: Professional services firms staffed at both ends of the city pair

corporate_links.claim: Austin's financial base includes Charles Schwab's trading technology centre, Dimensional Fund Advisors' headquarters, Visa's global IT centre and JPMorgan Chase, matching the sector that leads Edinburgh's economy.
corporate_links.caption: Financial and payments employers in Austin, the sector that leads Edinburgh

tourism.claim: American visitors made 964,339 trips to Scotland in 2024, making the United States Scotland's largest international source market by visits, nights and spend.
tourism.caption: Trips to Scotland from the United States, its largest overseas market

tourism.claim: American visitors spent £1,441 million in Scotland in 2024, accounting for 36% of all overseas visitor spend in the country.
tourism.caption: Spend in Scotland by visitors from the United States in a single year

tourism.claim: The City of Edinburgh received 5.05 million overnight tourism visits in 2024, worth £2,565 million in overnight spend.
tourism.caption: Overnight visits to Edinburgh from domestic and international visitors

tourism.claim: An estimated 2,604,404 tickets were issued across the 2025 Edinburgh Festival Fringe, for 3,893 shows in 301 venues with 62 countries represented on stage.
tourism.caption: Tickets issued across the world's largest arts festival, held every August

tourism.claim: South by Southwest drew participation of approximately 309,327 in Austin in March 2025, with attendees from 97 countries.
tourism.caption: Participation across SXSW and SXSW EDU in Austin in March

tourism.claim: Austin City Limits Music Festival contributed $534.8 million to the Austin economy in 2024, hosting 75,000 people a day at Zilker Park across two weekends.
tourism.caption: Contribution of the Austin City Limits festival to the city's economy

tourism.claim: Texas received 2,087,000 overseas visits in 2024, whose spending supported 45,620 jobs, making it the fourth-largest United States state for overseas visitor spending.
tourism.caption: Overseas visits to Texas, the fourth-highest of any US state
tourism.source_name: US National Travel and Tourism Office

diaspora.claim: The Scottish Government estimates that upwards of 40 million people worldwide consider themselves to have Scottish ancestry, against a home population of five and a half million.
diaspora.caption: People worldwide who consider themselves of Scottish ancestry

diaspora.claim: The 2020 United States Census recorded 5.3 million people claiming Scottish ancestry, some 1.6% of the United States population.
diaspora.caption: Americans claiming Scottish ancestry at the most recent census

diaspora.claim: 19% of American visitors travel to Scotland to see friends and relatives, with a further 73% visiting as holidaymakers.
diaspora.caption: Share of American visitors to Scotland travelling to see friends and relatives

diaspora.claim: Aside from Inner London, Edinburgh has a higher number of residents born in the United States, over 3,700, than any other city in the United Kingdom.
diaspora.caption: US-born residents of Edinburgh, more than any UK city outside Inner London

diaspora.claim: The 1990 census listed 36,854 people of Scottish descent in Texas, a community established by Scots arriving from 1825 onward.
diaspora.caption: People of Scottish descent recorded in Texas at the 1990 census

diaspora.claim: An annual Gathering of the Clans has been held at Salado in Bell County, Texas every November since 1961.
diaspora.caption: Texas has held an annual Scottish gathering since the early 1960s

education.claim: 3,090 students at the University of Edinburgh were domiciled in the United States on entry in session 2024/25, its second-largest overseas domicile after mainland China.
education.caption: US-domiciled students at the University of Edinburgh, its largest Western market

education.claim: 49,640 students were matriculated at the University of Edinburgh in session 2024/25, of whom 21,190 were domiciled overseas on entry.
education.caption: Students matriculated at the University of Edinburgh across the session

education.claim: Total enrolment at the University of Texas at Austin reached 55,000 in autumn 2025, the largest in the university's 142-year history.
education.caption: Total enrolment at the University of Texas at Austin, a record high
education.source_name: The University of Texas at Austin

education.claim: International enrolment at the University of Texas at Austin stood at 5,140 in 2025, some 9.3% of all students.
education.caption: International students enrolled at the University of Texas at Austin
education.source_name: The University of Texas at Austin

education.claim: The University of Edinburgh runs a reciprocal student exchange with the University of Texas at Austin, with published guidance for Edinburgh students spending one or two semesters on the Austin campus.
education.caption: A standing two-way student exchange already links the two cities

education.claim: Heriot-Watt University has around 27,000 students from 154 countries, with one third of its Scottish campus students coming from outside the United Kingdom.
education.caption: Students at Edinburgh-headquartered Heriot-Watt University worldwide

passenger_profile.claim: 229,000 United Kingdom residents visited Texas in 2024, making the United Kingdom the state's second-largest overseas visitor market.
passenger_profile.caption: UK residents visiting Texas in a single year, on the Governor's own figures
passenger_profile.source_name: Travel Texas, Office of the Governor of Texas

passenger_profile.claim: An estimated 50% of United Kingdom residents visiting Texas in 2024 travelled for vacation or holiday, with the balance travelling on business or for other purposes.
passenger_profile.caption: Share of UK visitors to Texas travelling for leisure rather than business
passenger_profile.source_name: Travel Texas, Office of the Governor of Texas

passenger_profile.claim: British Airways carried 247,562 passengers through Austin-Bergstrom in 2025, up 21.7% on the previous year, on the only nonstop link between Austin and the United Kingdom.
passenger_profile.caption: Passengers carried by the sole UK nonstop operator at Austin last year

passenger_profile.claim: KLM carried 76,254 passengers at Austin-Bergstrom in 2025, evidence of the Amsterdam hub routing European travellers use to reach Austin without a nonstop.
passenger_profile.caption: Passengers routed through the Amsterdam hub carrier at Austin last year

passenger_profile.claim: Dublin and Amsterdam were the most used international airports for flights to and from Scotland's main airports in 2023, both with just over 1.2 million passengers, and Transport Scotland notes both are hubs with extensive onward connections.
passenger_profile.caption: Scottish passengers using each of the two leading European connecting hubs

passenger_profile.claim: American Airlines has configured the Airbus A321XLR it selected for Edinburgh with 20 Flagship Suite lie-flat seats, 12 Premium Economy seats and 123 Main Cabin seats.
passenger_profile.caption: Lie-flat business seats on the narrowbody American picked for Edinburgh

airport_overview.claim: Edinburgh Airport welcomed a record 16,980,588 passengers in 2025, the first time any airport in Scotland has recorded such numbers.
airport_overview.caption: Record annual throughput at Edinburgh, an all-time high for any Scottish airport

airport_overview.claim: Edinburgh Airport handled 15.8m passengers in 2024, 10% more than in 2023.
airport_overview.caption: Passengers through Scotland's busiest airport the year before its record

airport_overview.claim: Edinburgh Airport has 37 airlines flying to 155 destinations, and recorded 120k aircraft movements in 2024.
airport_overview.caption: Destinations served from Edinburgh across thirty-seven operating airlines

airport_overview.claim: Edinburgh Airport operates a single runway of 2560m serving one terminal, infrastructure that already supports Boeing 787 and Airbus A321XLR transatlantic services.
airport_overview.caption: Runway length at Edinburgh, on the airport's published facts and figures

airport_overview.claim: Austin-Bergstrom International Airport handled 21,666,852 departing and arriving passengers in 2025, its third-busiest year on record.
airport_overview.caption: Passengers through Austin-Bergstrom, its third-highest annual total

airport_overview.claim: The Journey With AUS programme represents an estimated $5 billion investment in modernising and expanding Austin-Bergstrom International Airport.
airport_overview.caption: Estimated value of Austin's multi-year airport expansion programme

airport_overview.claim: Austin-Bergstrom completed its international arrivals improvements in 2025, adding 20,600 square feet of queuing, new baggage carousels and more Customs and Border Protection booths so that several international flights can be processed at once.
airport_overview.caption: Extra space added at Austin for international arrivals and customs

non_cannibalization.claim: There were 26 million air terminal passengers at Scottish airports in 2023, of which 55% travelled through Edinburgh, by far the largest single origin base in Scotland.
non_cannibalization.caption: Edinburgh's share of all Scottish airport passengers, on official statistics

non_cannibalization.claim: London Heathrow accounted for 25% of passengers on selected domestic routes to and from Edinburgh in 2023, and Transport Scotland notes these figures include passengers connecting onward to the rest of the world.
non_cannibalization.caption: Share of Edinburgh's selected domestic traffic routed through the London hub

non_cannibalization.claim: At Edinburgh Airport 51% of international leisure tourism was inbound in 2025, against 31% for the United Kingdom airport sector as a whole.
non_cannibalization.caption: Inbound share of Edinburgh international leisure travel, well above the UK norm

non_cannibalization.claim: Edinburgh Airport recorded 4,184,308 inbound passengers in 2025, a 40% increase since 2019, while outbound passengers fell 6% over the same period.
non_cannibalization.caption: Inbound passengers arriving into Scotland through Edinburgh last year

non_cannibalization.claim: After stripping out visitors who would have come to Scotland anyway, an estimated 3.6 million visitors in 2025 were attributed specifically to Edinburgh Airport, generating £1.8 billion of additional visitor spending.
non_cannibalization.caption: Visitors judged additional to Scotland because of Edinburgh Airport

case_study.claim: American Airlines launched daily seasonal Philadelphia to Edinburgh service on 23 May 2025, its first flights to Scotland since 2019 and a return to Edinburgh from a United States city other than New York.
case_study.caption: American reopened Edinburgh from a hub other than New York in 2025

case_study.claim: American Airlines selected New York JFK to Edinburgh, starting 8 March 2026, as the first international route for the Airbus A321XLR and the first United States deployment of the type across the Atlantic.
case_study.caption: Edinburgh was chosen for the first US transatlantic A321XLR route

case_study.claim: Aer Lingus opened Dublin to Nashville on 12 April 2025 with four weekly Airbus A321XLR flights on a nine-hour sector, with fares from EUR 499 return.
case_study.caption: A narrowbody opened a previously unserved US city from a European origin

case_study.claim: United Airlines returns to Glasgow on 9 May 2026 with daily seasonal Newark service on a 166-seat Boeing 737 MAX 8, the first scheduled United States airline service between Glasgow and the United States since 2019.
case_study.caption: Seats on the narrowbody United used to reopen a Scottish transatlantic route

case_study.claim: JetBlue launched daily seasonal Boston to Edinburgh service on 22 May 2025, its seventh transatlantic market from Boston.
case_study.caption: A second US carrier added Edinburgh from a non-New York hub in 2025
